    tsdst.modeling.predict¶

    tsdst.modeling.predict(X_test, X_train, Y_train, fit_mod, logit=True, interval='prediction', low_memory=False, lamda=0, level=0.95, logit_transform=False, logit_se_method='wald', *, covariance='sampling', penalize_intercept=False)[source]¶

    Calculate regression predictions with confidence or prediction intervals.

    Parameters:
    X_testarray-like

    Feature rows where predictions are required.

    X_trainarray-like

    Training feature matrix used to estimate coefficient covariance.

    Y_trainarray-like

    Training response values.

    fit_modfitted estimator

    Linear or binary logistic model.

    logitbool, optional

    Use logistic calculations when True. The default is True.

    interval{‘prediction’, ‘confidence’}, optional

    Linear prediction intervals include error variance for a new response; confidence intervals describe the fitted mean. The default is ‘prediction’. For logistic regression, ‘prediction’ emits a warning and returns a confidence interval for the response probability.

    low_memorybool, optional

    Retained argument passed to GenerateRegCov. The default is False.

    lamdafloat, optional

    Effective L2 penalty matching the fit. The default is zero.

    levelfloat, optional

    Interval coverage level between zero and one. The default is 0.95.

    logit_transformbool, optional

    Transform logistic predictions and both endpoints to probabilities. Otherwise return log-odds. The default is False.

    logit_se_method{‘wald’}, optional

    Logistic interval method. The default is ‘wald’. A delta-method interval is not implemented.

    covariance{‘sampling’, ‘curvature’}, optional

    Covariance interpretation. The default is ‘sampling’.

    penalize_interceptbool, optional

    Match the fitted model’s intercept penalty. The default is False.

    Returns:
    resultpandas.DataFrame

    Columns yhat, lower_int, and upper_int contain predictions and bounds.

    Notes

    OLS intervals use Student t critical values with n-p residual degrees of freedom. Logistic Wald intervals use normal critical values on the linear predictor. Transforming both endpoints through the inverse logit gives probability confidence bounds.

    Intervals for penalized fits are approximations. Sampling covariance describes variation of the shrunken estimator and does not remove its bias for unpenalized population parameters. Curvature intervals use a local Gaussian-prior interpretation with an estimated noise scale when needed.
